leftEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
leftEvidence.title: Hebrews asks who rebelled and why they could not enter

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Hebrews quotes the psalm’s “today,” warns against an unbelieving heart, and asks who rebelled after hearing.
points.right: Jude reminds readers that the Lord saved a people out of Egypt and afterward destroyed those who did not believe.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Those who sinned fell in the wilderness, and the conclusion names unbelief as the reason they could not enter.
points.right: The whole wilderness history is compressed into rescue followed by judgment on unbelief.

payload.posture: Hebrews and Jude both turn wilderness unbelief after deliverance into warning for later hearers.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Jude recalls rescue from Egypt followed by destruction of unbelievers

payload.tension: Hebrews develops Psalm 95 and rest at length; Jude compresses rescue and later destruction into one reminder.
payload.title: Two later warnings from rescue followed by unbelief
